comparison.denominator: Codex complete episode; both episodes consist of one first submission
comparison.conclusion: Vector costs less and uses less agent wall time in this pair, but the saving is below 20% and its blinded code score is one point lower. This pair does not establish the study objective.

blindedCodeReview.method: Blinded static exact-source review with two supplied independent screenshots per submission

both: Changed default data directories can leave retained v1 history undiscovered when upgrading without an explicit DATA_DIR; this is not deletion.
Full stream buffering and untested storage/pipe failures and immediate restart overlap limit reliability evidence.
vector: A cancellation/crash window can leave the legacy job status running after workflow recovery marks it cancelled.
Persistence after spawn and stream/completion failures can escape child ownership or skip live-slot cleanup.
codex: Small, muted metadata/history/output text limits readability.
The start-persistence guard does not explicitly await child reaping; logged completion failures can leave persisted running work awaiting restart.

blindedCodeReview.limitation: No critical finding was established within static source and screenshot coverage. The reviewer did not independently execute either app or its authored tests. This is not production security, reliability, or usability assurance.

patchFormatObservation.classification: Patch-envelope formatting failure identified in controller metadata
patchFormatObservation.note: The retry is an observation, not a causal estimate of token or cost savings from an envelope-only change.

accountingCheckpoint.scope: Historical checkpoint at settlement of this development-task pair
accountingCheckpoint.note: The holdout was active after this checkpoint. These figures do not report the current study bill.

interpretationLimits: One adaptive development-task pair before and after is not independent causal evidence.
The candidate bundles optional browser-focus metadata and changed verification guidance; their individual effects are not isolated.
The corrected browser instrument is shared by both candidate arms and the free baseline reevaluations, while the original baseline paid repair was induced by the earlier checker.
No conclusion about held-out task quality or cost is established here.

publication.note: Both original first-submission source archives are published byte-for-byte; no normalized review copy replaces them.

sanitization.activityLimitations: Observed CLI bytes are not model tokens or cost. Missing fields have no observations, not measured zero size. Error and repeated-input counts do not alone establish waste or product failure.

browserProvisioningDeviation.observation: Vector authored scripts/browser-check.mjs importing the provided Playwright module and launching Chrome directly; three execution references were verified in the completed command records.
browserProvisioningDeviation.interpretation: The agent-owned checks did not all stay within the common browser client despite the task wording. Costs and delivery checks remain recorded, but these observations are exploratory and do not establish strict shared-client protocol adherence.
browserProvisioningDeviation.instrumentInstructionConflict: The old runner explicitly advertised PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE and CHROME_PATH alongside a common-client-only helper instruction. This is conflicting instrumentation, not assumed agent misconduct.
